Sennecke - Strong Side Wing vs Off Wing

Apologies if I’m not the most knowledgeable hockey person, so please correct me if I’m wrong about anything down below, but I just wanted to talk about Beckett a little bit and how the Ducks are deploying him, since they’ve been playing him on his off wing for the first two games rather than his strong side wing, which is what he played all last season.

For those who don’t know, there are two sides that a winger can play on: their strong-side wing or their off wing. Strong-side is when you’re playing on your natural side. Think left handed shot playing on the left hand side. Players usually prefer their strong side because they often get to receive and carry the puck on their forehand, which is usually better for transporting the puck and passing. Off wing is the opposite, with the case of Sennecke being a right shot while playing on the left wing. The reason you play the off wing is to get better angles for shots, whether their wristers or one-timers (hence why Gauthier plays right wing as a left handed shot).

I think it’s interesting that Beckett is being deployed on the off wing this year since it may give some insight into how the Ducks want to develop him. Last year, he played exclusively on his strong side as a right winger, which helped him become an elite puck transporter through the neutral zone (he was in the 98th percentile for creating zone entries) and a solid playmaker (37 assists). However, he also clearly had a scoring touch with 23 goals of all varieties, including goals around the crease and shots from distance with his 95+ MPH shot.

Thus, it’s interesting that this year, they’re having him play on the left wing. By playing him on his off-side, it seems that they’re choosing to value his shooting abilities over his puck transportation and playmaking skills. This could be because he’s actually pretty decent on his backhand or because Granlund is the playmaker on his line, but it’s an interesting choice since this may steer his development to be more of a shooter than a playmaker.

Curious on if anyone has any further insights onto this, or if anyone just has any other thoughts in general about how they’re using/developing him. Sennecke has sky high potential and could be just about anything on offense (whether it’s a play maker, a shooter, a net front presence, or maybe all 3), but I always thought he would be better developed on the right than the left since his puck transportation on his forehand is so elite.

Why Leo Carlsson is worth close to $18 million.

Leo Carlsson started this season on fire. He had 41 points in his first 33 games. That's on pace for 102 points over 82 games. But he got injured after 33 games and tried to play through it. He had just 3 points in his next 11 games. After it was evident he could not play through his injury he decided to get surgery and missed 12 games as well as a chance to play at the Olympics for Sweden. In the final 26 games of the season he had 23 points after returning from injury.

I do think that if he stays healthy he can have a 100+ point season which in today's NHL is worth at least 15 million. The NHL salary cap will increase at least 9 million dollars after next season which will help ease the burden. I think over the length of this contract the $18m will be fair value. The injury Leo suffered this season is not the kind of injury that is expected to be a nagging injury that will handicap him in the future. 

One thing that also helps the Ducks is that if the Ducks match the offer, there will be no trade protection on his deal. That means if Leo is unwilling to sign an extension in his fifth year, the Ducks will not be handicapped in moving him to get a good trade. 

I do not think Pat Verbeek handled this contract negotiation perfectly and should have signed him before July 1. And, he absolutely should never have cut communication when the season started. That being said, this is not a nightmare scenario. It's a 3 million ish overpayment. 

If the Ducks can sign Mintyukov, Hinds and Gauthier to a combined 22 million dollar cap hit as well as find a way to move off of Vatrano they will be under the cap next season.

As previously stated, the Salary cap is expected to rise from 104m to 113m following the 2027-28 season. Add on the fact that Kreider's 6.5m and Killorn's 6.25m will be coming off the books following this season. They will be able to manage the cap beyond this year. They will have to replace those players but the Ducks have a deep prospect pool on the wings. 

Next seasons RFA/UFA class is not as threatening as this years was. RFA's include Tristan Luneau, Tim Washe, Nathan Gaucher, and everyone's favorite Drew Helleson. Ufa's include Kreider and Killorn. There is also Nesterenko who is set to be a UFA group 6. Oher people will be able to explain what that is better than I could. My point is they shouldn't have too much difficulty fitting players under the cap for the 2027-28 season. That is of course assuming Verbeek can fit Gauthier, Mintyukov, and Hinds to 22 million which I think is possible if only because Gauthier does not have the offer sheet eligible leverage that Leo had.

Beckett Sennecke will become a UFA the same season that Granlund's $7 million comes off the books Combine that with however much the Salary cap increases and you have him locked up.

Ducks will match Leo Carlsson's offer and they will still be a future Stanley Cup Contender.

text:
[HockeyStatCards] 2026-10-04 GameScore Impact Card vs Florida

Reposting with just Sunday's game since I mistakenly added Friday's after it had already been posted.

For anyone looking for a primer on what's going on with these charts:

Dom Luszczyszyn developed [Game Score for hockey](https://hockey-graphs.com/2016/07/13/measuring-single-game-productivity-an-introduction-to-game-score/) almost a decade ago, which was a model that essentially aggregated different individual player stats (or "counting stats" i.e. goals, primary/secondary assists, hits, blocks, faceoffs, etc) and weighted them based on how much they were estimated to contribute to a team's success (the idea was to emulate similar stats in baseball/basketball). The result, a player's "Game Score", was an approximation of how effective a player is in a given game.

Over the years, the model has been updated to take more info into account when calculating a player's impact, including adding weight to possession/shot suppression stats [expected goals (xG) for and against](https://archive.is/6KFPC) to paint a better picture of how a player contributes to their team's offense or defense while that player is on the ice. More recently, Dom's model was [reworked to present players' offensive and defensive "ratings" above or below average](https://archive.is/lmsW7) and to focus more on expected goals than Corsi/Fenwick-derived possession (i.e. shot quality vs shot quantity, put simply).

Essentially, the cards pull game data from [Natural Stat Trick](https://www.naturalstattrick.com), run the data through the Game Score model/algorithm to assign weight to the stats, and visualize the results, (i.e. a player's relative on-ice "impact") in these bar charts. Generally, the "Production" categories pull from the counting stats mentioned in the first paragraph, "Play Driving" accounts for a player's 5v5 goals and xG (for and against) relative to team and league averages, with roughly the same stats accounted for under "Special Teams" but for PP and PK respectively. I'm not 100% sure how Quality of Competition is derived here but it usually has to do with a player's ice time spent playing with or against the players with the most usage in a given game.

Some of these data points can be pretty dynamic based on how team and league averages change over the season, so there's an argument to be made that these "impacts" don't say all that much in a vacuum. However, as the season goes on, you can start to see some neat stuff from players' cumulative Game Scores, and in the meantime, it's fun to see whether your eye test matches or refutes what's happening according to the model.

The data can be presented differently, and is a bit easier to poke around in on the [HockeyStatCards website](https://www.hockeystatcards.com) if you feel like digging a bit deeper yourself. For example, as of 2026 you can toggle a "Table" view on the Hockey Stat Cards site to see the each player's raw values for each category in a given game.

**TL; DR: Game Score above 0 (right) = good, Game Score below 0 (left) = bad.**

Viel gets a 5-year $12.5 million contract and Johnston gets a 3-year $6 million one. They both successfully use the Ducks as a stepping stone to advance their careers.

The Ducks need to be better at seeing the value we build and reinvesting in it. I worry that we still see these players as unwanted diamonds in the rough when it comes to contract negotiations. Unfortunately we lose our leverage when we polish the diamonds because everyone else suddenly sees the value in them. If we don't reinvest, they walk and we let other teams reap the benefits of our scouting and development.

Proposal: The Cutter Contract

We all know the situation we're in but I've spent the last couple of days looking at the options and now that we know exactly what Mintyukov will cost we know what we can pay Cutter even if we retain Leo, which we absolutely should do. Here's how I see it:  
  
The following lineup costs $90.18 million:

Kreider / Carlsson / ***Gauthier***  
Killorn / Granlund / Sennecke  
Wahlberg / Poehling / Vatrano  
Greer / Washe / Colangelo

LaCombe / Luneau  
Mintyukov / Jensen  
Moore / Helleson

Dostal / Brossoit

Scratch: Malott / Nesterenko / ***Hinds***

I've put Gauthier and Hinds in bold and italics because they both need to be re-signed. The cap is $104 million so that leaves just under $14 million to play with. If the Ducks signed Cutter to a two-year, $24 million deal and Hinds to a three year, $3.5 million deal that would bring the salary to $103.34m. Under the cap.

The problem would be kicked down the road a bit but eventually Terry would return from IR meaning the Ducks would need to clear $7 million in space to activate him. That could mean trading Kreider, assuming the entire roster is healthy and other players aren't on LTIR by then.

If you add $7 million (Terry) to that salary but subtract $6.5 million (Kreider) then you're still under the cap at $103.84 million. It's doable.

Now, why sign Cutter to a two year deal? Because a year from now you can sign him to a seven year extension at BIG money. Kreider, Killorn, Vatrano, Granlund and Jensen would all be off the books before that extension kicked in during the 2028-29 season and by then the cap is expected to be $123 million per team. Plus, guys like McQueen, Klepov, Solberg and others should be ready for NHL minutes by then to help save money on depth positions.

Here's why we'll match—but probably lose Mintyukov

**Salary cap numbers to know**

* 2026-2027: $104m upper limit
* 2027-2028: $113m upper limit
* 2028-2029: $123m upper limit

**Match the offer sheet (we'd have $17m remaining for this season)**

* Leo becomes the highest paid player in the league
* He gets a NMC
* He'll be a UFA at age 26

**Let Leo walk (we'd have $35m remaining)**

* We get 4 first-round picks over the next four years (probably mid-late picks)
* We reallocate the $18m cap hit & use the picks to build through trades

**Ultimately, I think we match the offer sheet — but we wait the full 7 days so that Philly has tied up its cap space.** 

This helps us figure out a deal for Cutter (He & Terry have the same agent, Kurt Overhardt). Probably 8 years x $12.5m

Unfortunately, I think this means we lose Mintyukov to another offer sheet. For example, 2 years at $7m would be prohibitive for us, and somebody probably takes a swing. The comp would be a 1st and a 3rd. 

In all, we'd have just $4.5 million to build out the roster for next season. So, I'm not optimistic about making the playoffs in 2026-2027.

But, in 2027-2028, we'll have $12.75 million coming off the books when Kreider and Killorn's deals expire. And with the cap rising by $9 million, we'll effectively have \~$21 million for Sennecke's next contract and bolstering the roster.

Leo's offer sheet definitely makes roster building harder, but with the money that's being thrown around, $18m AAV isn't *that* much higher than a $14-15m AAV. Essentially, this costs us a 2nd-3rd pairing defenseman (and look—we just jettisoned Zellweger).

Ultimately, I think we can stomach this deal because of the depth in our prospect pool. It's definitely an overpay and the deal looks shocking today. But in 4-5 years, it should be fair value as a percentage of the cap (maybe 14%).

Realistically, our contending window only opens in the next 2 years. So, we need Luneau, Solberg, McQueen, and Klepov to step up over the next couple years.

Altogether, I think this encourages PVB to sign our other RFAs sooner. This isn't the disaster everybody's making it out to be, but it'll definitely be harder to compete against a team like Montreal which locked down Hutson ($8.85m AAV) and Demidov for ($9.15m AAV) early.

I am scared of turning into Maple Leafs West though, with big money tied up in just 4-5 guys.

Look Ahead at the 2028-29 Anaheim Ducks Roster

TL; DR - The Ducks are screwed by Carlsson's greed for this season and probably for the 2027-28 season as well. But in 2028-29 they're in a good place to have a solid roster with options to add veterans to the core you see above to upgrade and improve.  
  
We all know what the roster for this year looks like and we know we are waiting two years for Vatrano, Killorn, Granlund, Jensen and Kreider to clear our books. So let's look ahead at the 2028-29 roster and see what we have, what we need and how much we'll have to spend:

**FORWARDS**

1. *Gauthier* / Carlsson / *Sennecke*
2. *Wahlberg* / McQueen / Klepov
3. Nordmark / Poehling / Terry
4. Malott / *Washe* / Greer

**DEFENSE**

1. LaCombe / *Luneau*
2. Mintyukov / Solberg
3. *Hinds* / *Moore*

**GOALIE**

1. Dostal
2. *Clara*

**HEALTHY SCRATCHES**

* *Warren*
* *Gaucher*
* Pettersson

  
12 of those 23 players are already under contract. The other 10 will be RFAs between now and the start of that season. One player, Nikita Klepov, will be on an ELC that season and can make a maximum of $1.775 million per season so I've set that as his price for the sake of argument.

  
Salary cap: $123m

Cost of players already signed: $63.34m

The point is this - yes, the Ducks are screwed by Carlsson's greed for this season and probably for the 2027-28 season as well. But in 2028-29 they're in a good place to have a solid roster with options to add veterans to the core you see above to upgrade and improve.

I think the problem lies in seeing the value we built and reinvesting in it accordingly. We have a pattern of low balling our top talent and dragging out the negotiation process, letting players like Carlsson and Minty get huge offer sheets and alienating players like McTavish and Zegras. It seems like we're great at evaluating players and picking up talent when it's cheap but struggle with reevaluating value when it comes time for negotiations. The market is dictating that we are undervaluing our players.

If we don't see the value in our players and reinvest earlier, they walk and we let other teams reap the benefits of our scouting and development.

text:
Choosing Door #2 - Letting Carlsson Go

For the sake of looking at the options, here's the argument for letting the Flyers have Carlsson and taking the compensation.

  
**1. The compensation:**  
**-** Philadelphia's 1st round pick in 2027  
**-** Philadelphia's 1st round pick in 2028  
**-** Philadelphia's 1st round pick in 2029  
**-** Philadelphia's 1st round pick in 2030

Ducks would have their own 1st round pick and the Flyers 1st round pick in each of the next four years as well as three 2nd round picks in 2027 - their own, the Blues and the Red Wings. They'd have serious draft capital to make trades with for the next four off-seasons including what's left of this one. 

**2. The replacements:**  
The Ducks could trade for Elias Pettersson to replace Carlsson's minutes as top line center until McQueen is (hopefully) ready to take that spot. Pettersson is owed $11.6 million for the next five seasons with a NMC the entire time so it's a risky move but he turns 28 this season and is at least a competent option that we know is available via trade.

The Ducks could also push to get Dylan Larkin. He's owed $8.7 million for the next five seasons with a NMC the entire time as well. He turns 30 later this month.

There may be other centers available we are unaware of and, if so, the Ducks would certainly have the draft capital and the prospects to make it happen.

**3. The revenge:**  
The Ducks can now be aggressive and offer sheet other players at the expense of their own draft capital knowing they have the Flyers 1st round picks in each of the next four years as well as the Blues and Red Wings 2nd round picks in 2027. Matvei Michkov is a RFA next summer and in 2028 Porter Martone will be a RFA. Re-signing Zegras and Drysdale in addition to Carlsson could put a squeeze on the Flyers

Or, the Ducks could make a push for Jason Robertson this summer. Or Conner Bedard. Or Adam Fantilli. Or they could offer sheet a RFA in 2027. They would have many options at their disposal should they chose to use them.

**4. The reset:**  
The Ducks could also learn from this and reset their rebuild/timeline. We thought the rebuild was ending but if they lose Carlsson, McTavish, Zellweger this summer (in addition to Trouba, Carlson, Gudas, Johnston, Viel and Harkins) on the heels of losing Drysdale and Zegras over the last two years...and if all they have to show for all of those departures is a ton of draft picks/prospects, Ryan Poehling and Cutter Gauthier...then they could reset the rebuild, suck ass this season while playing a LOT of young guys and move forward building the team around Sennecke, Gauthier, McQueen, LaCombe, Mintyukov, Dostal and the many young prospects still in the system. They could then hope that one of the MANY draft picks they have in future years yields a franchise center or allows them to trade to acquire one.

Honestly, when it's all said and done this is probably the best option for the franchise. It sucks, and it's going to suck seeing Carlsson thrive in Philadelphia (before he hopefully walks as a UFA at 26) but committing $18 million to a 21 year old and leaving yourself exposed for offer sheets on other players in the future might be worse when it's all said and done.

Less Lecturing, More Conversation

A few of us, myself included, have been worried about the Ducks offseason for a few weeks. We saw the lack of progress towards re-signing a single member of the right side of the defense, the lack of progress towards re-signing any of the pending RFAs and the complete lack of denial that Mason McTavish was on the market and we were worried. We said as much in here as both comments and posts.

...and we got downvoted into oblivion for it. Multiple posts were created telling us to "calm down" and to "quit being Doomers". We were mocked for criticizing GM Pat Verbeek and were reminded that it wasn't July 1st yet numerous times, as if we were unaware of the calendar. One post even told us we couldn't complain until the first preseason game in September!

Most of us took those downvotes and moved on with our day because we believed what we said. Some of us deleted posts and comments because of the downvotes and the numerous replies mocking us or shouting us down for having the audacity to be concerned.

Clearly, we were right to be concerned. It's been an absolute disaster of an offseason by any measure. There have been no players of value added to the roster from outside the organization. We've lost our top pairing RD, our 2nd pairing RD, our 3rd pairing RD and our 3rd pairing LD. We've lost three fourth line players. We've lost our 2nd line center and could be six days away from losing our top line center. All we have added is depth guys, grit and draft picks.

So please, in the future, when people express concern about the path the team is on argue the facts with them but do not downvote them. Don't reply just to tell them to calm down. Do not remind them of the calendar. Same goes if someone is happy about something - let them be happy about it! We don't need to tell people they're wrong for feeling the way they do if that's all you're going to say.

We're all Ducks fans here and we all want the same thing - a second Cup for the Ducks. If people are concerned about the coaching, the management or the players let them be concerned and either scroll past it or engage them in conversation about why you feel differently. But the time for people telling others to calm down or that they're being a doomer for being concerned should be officially over at this point.

text:
Fire Verbeek.  Fire Solomon.

Regardless of whether Leo ends up going or staying, I hope this situation leaves a lasting, learning, effect on this organization.  This team has been considered one of the toughest teams to work with by player agents for a long time and this leads back to the Bob Murray days.  That hasn't changed, it exacerbated the issue when Verbeek came onboard and constantly holding guys like Terry, Dostal, McTavish, Zegras, and Drysdale until the very last minute.  With teams around the league approaching their negotiating tactics to cater more towards players, it feels like we are behind the times on that front.  Now that players have a louder voice in negotiations, this is how we got to where we are now.  Verbeek f--ked around and found out, that much is true.  I just hope the Samuelis are watching this unfold and taking action when the dust settles.  It's time for this team to review their process of conducting business.  This is why players don't want to be here and this is why younger players might not be loyal to the club.  I hope the Samuelis do the right thing and step in.  Both Verbeek and Solomon need to go.
